summary: Today’s pulse tracks Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes, Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel to be towed away from Ibiza, and ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are against, canadian, and canadians. In the background, Sales for Biden memoir fall far short of books by Obama and Clinton and 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Spanish PM and rivals rally supporters in final pitch for votes
headlines.description: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez wants to defy the polls, and his main rivals accuse him of not telling the truth and of "betrayal".

headlines.title: Capsized tanker carrying 7,000 tonnes of diesel to be towed away from Ibiza
headlines.description: There are fears of a major oil spillage off Ibiza but the ship's fuel tanks are so far intact.

headlines.title: ‘Abusive and insulting to Canadians’: campaign to oust US ambassador presented to parliament
headlines.description: Hundreds of thousands of Canadians call for Pete Hoekstra to be declared ‘persona non grata’ A petition signed by nearly 290,000 Canadians calling on Mark Carney’s government to oust Pete Hoekstra as US ambassador to Canada was formally presented to the House of Commons on Thursday, a sign of the strained relations between the neighboring countries. Elizabeth May, a Canadian Green party member, originally opened the petition for signatures in July 2026 after a woman from Calgary sponsored it. The petition requests that the Canadian government declare Hoekstra “persona non grata” due to his “US” diplomatic interference in Canadian domestic affairs”.

headlines.title: Sales for Biden memoir fall far short of books by Obama and Clinton
headlines.description: Promise Me, America, which has lukewarm reviews from critics, sold about 21,000 copies during its first week on sale Joe Biden’s memoir Promise Me, America debuted with modest sales and lackluster reviews, selling about 21,000 copies during its first week on sale, according to Circana. It sold well enough to top the New York Times nonfiction bestseller list, but didn’t approach the level of memoirs by such predecessors as Barack Obama and Bill Clinton.

headlines.title: 'We couldn't give up that easily': Marching bands scramble to cover costs after Thanksgiving parade rearranged
headlines.description: Stormy weather in New York City prompted organisers to push back the Macy's parade by two days - leaving some musicians stuck.

headlines.title: Graham Thorpe’s widow takes legal action against NHS trust after inquest
headlines.description: Former England Test cricketer was diagnosed with anxiety and depression before he took his own life in 2024 The wife of Graham Thorpe, the former England cricketer who took his own life, has started legal proceedings against an NHS trust after an inquest identified “failings” in his mental health care. Thorpe died aged 55 in August 2024 in Surrey. His wife, Amanda, has lodged a personal injury claim at the high court against Surrey and Borders Partnership NHS foundation trust which was involved in his care, the Telegraph reported. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org . In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org

headlinePool.title: DWP ‘cyber incident’ knocks almost all pensions and benefits systems offline
headlinePool.description: Department for Work and Pensions urges people to be alert to scams related to outage and contact helpline with urgent difficulties Tell us: have you been affected by the DWP ‘cyber incident’ Benefits and pensions claimants have faced chaos after the system was hit by a “serious cyber incident”, fuelling concerns about the UK government’s ability to defend itself against malicious attacks. The government took its portal down late on Thursday after detecting “unusual activity”, meaning anyone trying to check their state pension, make an application for disability benefits or claim universal credit on Friday was unable to do so.

headlinePool.title: Weary of war but with no sign of backing down, Kyiv faces another punishing winter
headlinePool.description: Ukraine settles in for another devastating winter as the questions persists: how will it all end?

headlinePool.title: Police suspect criminals robbed fans at Manchester gig disrupted by ‘unknown substance’
headlinePool.description: Police are working with agencies across Europe after similar incidents occurred at two other Don Toliver concerts A group of organised criminals are believed to have carried out robberies during Don Toliver’s Manchester concert, where an “unknown substance” was released , police have said, with similar incidents having occurred at another two of the US rapper’s gigs in Europe. Greater Manchester police said they were working to identify the suspects and the substance involved during the incident at the Co-op Live Arena on Sunday evening.

headlinePool.title: Zelensky criticises 'strange' Trump-Putin friendship in BBC interview
headlinePool.description: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is not pushing Russia hard enough in peace talks to end the war.

headlinePool.title: The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children
headlinePool.description: FBI estimates thousands of people identify as members, or recent members, of group linked to indecent images of girls and blackmail It sounds benign: the Com, short for the Community. But crime agencies around the world warn that it is far from that and the young cybercriminals involved are causing havoc and putting children at chilling, sickening risk. Beau-Jack Mensforth was jailed by a UK judge on Friday for his activities as part of the Com. He was one individual operating from his bedroom in north-east England, but there are probably thousands more like him and parents are being urged by police to be aware and to check their children’s devices.

headlinePool.title: Labour row over Rosebank deepens as dozens of MPs warn PM not to block oilfield
headlinePool.description: Warning of ‘lights out for Labour in Scotland’ as Burnham faces choice between warring factions over North Sea drilling project Dozens of Labour MPs in favour of Rosebank are putting pressure on the prime minister not to block the North Sea oilfield, warning that doing so could spell “lights out for Labour in Scotland”. As many as 80 pro-drilling MPs are considering writing their own letter to Andy Burnham after nearly 100 of their colleagues called on the prime minister not to allow the project to proceed . Scottish Labour leader Michael Marra has also reiterated his support for Rosebank, cautioning that “working-class people in vocational jobs” were threatened by the decline of the North Sea basin.

headlinePool.title: UK man jailed for online blackmail of vulnerable girls around the world
headlinePool.description: Beau-Jack Mensforth, 20, part of a group known as the Com, coerced girls into self-harm, making indecent images of themselves and physically harming pets The Com: the global cybercrime network posing a ‘chilling threat’ to children A 20-year-old man from north-east England has been jailed for blackmailing vulnerable girls around the world, prompting a senior police officer to urge parents to regularly check their children’s devices. Beau-Jack Mensforth admitted 17 offences of making and distributing indecent photographs of children, blackmail, and participating in the activities of an organised crime group.

headlinePool.title: Google told to halt Belgium datacentre construction over lack of planning permit
headlinePool.description: Greenpeace publishes report showing tech firm is continuing to build despite planning appeal still unresolved Belgian authorities have ordered Google to halt construction work on a large datacentre in the south of the country because the US tech firm’s requests to modify the original terms of the planning permission did not have approval. “Inspectors visited the site and observed that the building was almost finished, with the structural work completed, even though the permit had been refused,” Raphaël Stokis, a Wallonia regional official, told the public broadcaster RTBF .

headlinePool.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader convicted over further 123 deaths
headlinePool.description: Paul Mackenzie is found guilty of killing his followers, weeks after being jailed for the mass murder of children.
